metrics.method: Full history read end to end: 143 message ids, 131 messages plus 10 service events, 2026-08-03 to 2026-09-24 (ids 73 and 127 are absent from the export — 127 sits exactly between the client's Zelle request and Mayson's tag of billing, likely deleted). client_questions_total counts distinct client messages that required a substantive ALTR reply (direct questions, instructions, offers and bulk content handovers), collapsing same-minute bursts on one topic into one item. unanswered_over_24h = the 8/3 content library link (never acknowledged, 53d), the 8/19 stop-chatting instruction (never, 37d), the 9/10 5000+ photo handover (never, 15d) and the 9/12 squirting set (38h to a three-word thank-you covering two handovers). The 9/22 payment request is excluded on a technicality — it was answered at 20h55m — but was never resolved. max_team_silence_days is the longest gap between consecutive ALTR outbound messages: 2026-08-17 19:31 (Michelle) to 2026-08-26 19:17 (Stephski), and the message that broke it was an invoice chase. promises_made counts explicit forward commitments by ALTR staff; kept = a delivered, visible result (intros, the 8/3 release send-out, the 8/12 trailer, invoicing starting 8/15, the custom domain build, the 9/14 pre-invoice heads-up, the 8/31 receipt confirmation, the 8/30 pause ultimatum which produced payment); lapsed = no result and no admission; one promise (the 9/24 pull-from-her-drives commitment) is still pending and counted in neither.

what_client_wanted: Her collab scenes released on time at 7pm LA — her stated number-one priority from day one, with a five-drop calendar pinned on 8/3 and the standing time she confirmed herself: "Yes 7pm for all releases" (2026-08-12). Aug 17, Aug 24 and Aug 29 have no result, no confirmation and no written admission, and she has never complained about a single miss.

Her content pulled from HER storage and actually posted — proposed politely on 2026-09-10 ("Would it be possible to take stuff from my Dropbox instead?"), refused on 9/11, and finally demanded on 2026-09-24: "I’m not uploading to yours!! Why would I, I have 5000 + videos in my own that I have already organised".

More Instagram footprint, while keeping control of her own accounts — she asked unprompted on 2026-08-31 ("Would it possible to start more instas for me?" / "I’m already running a lot myself") and again signalled the boundary on 2026-09-16 ("I have 3 but just run them myself"). Access to her accounts is a trust milestone to her, not an admin task.

To be on top of leaks and impersonators — "Let me know what I need to do to get on top of my leaks" (2026-08-12), and on day one, prefaced with an apology, the alannaworldx0 takedown. She was promised weekly reports and has had one in 44 days; the takedown has never been confirmed in 53 days.

To shoot customs in volume — offered twice unprompted ("Any new customs or try to sell heaps I’ll do them in the next few days", 2026-08-15; "Any new customs?", 2026-08-26), declined both times, no sales figure ever reported, and she has not offered a third time.
what_worked: Ollie's week-one page audit and campaign restructure earned the only unqualified praise in the account's history — "Loving the chatting so far" / "It sounds so good" (Alanna, 2026-08-08). He logged in within an hour of the intro, explained the Tip $5 campaign mechanic before she could be surprised by it, and gave her a real opinion on her trailer strategy. That is the standard the account has been falling away from ever since.

Same-day, specific release check-ins built visible trust while they lasted — "Hey @alannaapow the lily and francis 3some is going live today right?" (Ollie, 2026-08-10) and "what time is the ass worship going out today? 7pm PST?" (2026-08-12) each drew an immediate "Thanks so much" / "Thankyou!". Both drops landed. The three drops that got no check-in are the three with no result.

The 2026-09-24 recovery was the best-handled moment anyone has produced here: no defensiveness, no policy defence, resolution in four minutes from the owner's first sight of it — Derrek "yes we can easily do this" / "makes 0 difference to us", Mica "yeah we can pull from your drives" / "just didn’t have them here, apologies!". She kept sending content links in the same thread rather than going quiet.

Stephski's billing craft, specifically the pre-invoice cash-flow heads-up ("your invoice will be sent tomorrow, so it would be great if you could initiate a OF withdrawl today", 2026-09-14) and the first dated, pre-emptive chase in the account's history ("Tomorrow is day 7 since recieving invoice so just wanted to bump", 2026-09-21) — which produced her first ever unprompted attempt to pay, the day after.
top_fix: Give the account one named owner who posts a dated weekly recap in the client thread — what shipped, what is next with dates, what we need from her, and every open item with its age — and who reads the thread before anyone sends a templated ask into it. Every failure on this account is a symptom of the same absence: five bulk content handovers with no confirmation, three missed scene drops, a 27-day empty release calendar, a 53-day-old takedown never closed, a payment request that only reached billing because a chatter happened to tag them, and a 38-day blocker that was trivially fixable and survived five weeks purely because nobody with authority ever looked at the oldest open item. A weekly written recap makes the age of each item visible to us before it becomes visible to her, and it is the only change that would have removed the need for her to shout in capitals and tag the owner to get a four-minute answer.
